CampaignContactEngagement.description:
A single per-contact engagement row for a campaign, as returned by
`GET /apps/api/v1/newsletters/{id}/contacts`.

**Note:** with `_mode=download` the row uses `first_name` and
`last_name` in place of the combined `name` field.

event_count.description:
Number of times the selected event occurred (e.g. number of opens
or clicks). Returned as a numeric string.

max_event_time.description:
Last time the selected event occurred for this contact, formatted
as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`.

min_event_time.description:
First time the selected event occurred for this contact, formatted
as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`.

name.description:
Contact name (may be `null`). Replaced by `first_name`/`last_name`
when `_mode=download` is used.

CampaignCreate.description:
Payload for creating a campaign through `POST /apps/api/v1/newsletters`
(no `clone` query parameter). The `campaign` property is required: it
marks the newsletter as a campaign and carries campaign-specific metadata.

campaign.description:
Campaign-specific metadata. Required marker for the create flow;
send `{}` to accept the defaults. Campaigns are always created as
`DRAFT`: to schedule one, call
`PUT /apps/api/v1/campaigns/{id}/schedule` after creating it.

status.description:
Optional. Any value other than `DRAFT` is ignored for the
resulting status.

html_body.description:
HTML body. Unless the account policy says otherwise, a campaign can
only be sent if the body contains the CAN-SPAM placeholders
`[[account:business]]`, `[[account:address_1]]`,
`[[account:city]]`, `[[account:postal_code]]`,
`[[account:country]]` and an unsubscribe link
`<a href="[[unsubscribe_link]]">`; otherwise the send ends in
`FAILED` with reason `one_or_more_can_spam_tags_are_missing`.

segment_id.description: Segment ID (optional; omit to target the whole list)

name.description: Campaign name (must be unique per account)

sender_id.description: Sender ID (must reference a verified sender)

type.description: Newsletter type. Always `CAMPAIGN` for this payload.

scheduled_time.description: Scheduled date (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`, local to the campaign timezone)

custom_fields.description:
Custom fields keyed by the field's `place_holder`. Each value type
depends on the custom field type: string (for `string`/`text`
fields) or boolean (for `bool` fields).

contact_added_to_list.description: Flag indicating if the contact was added to the list

custom_fields.description:
Custom fields keyed by the field's `place_holder`. Each value type
depends on the custom field type: string (for `string`/`text`
fields) or boolean (for `bool` fields).

admin_only.description: Flag indicating if the field is admin-only

mode.description: Field visibility mode. Always `ADMIN` when set.

is_pinned.description: Whether the list is pinned ("0" or "1")

NewsletterUpdate.description:
Payload for `PUT /apps/api/v1/newsletters/{id}`. Omitted newsletter
fields are overwritten with `null`, so send the complete model. The
server requires at least one of `campaign` or `autoresponder` in
`instance_in`, otherwise the request is silently ignored (returns
`200 OK` with no persistence).
When updating `name`, `id` must also be duplicated inside `instance_in`
(the server's duplicate-name check reads it from the body, not the URL).

autoresponder.description:
Required when updating an autoresponder-type newsletter. Mutually
exclusive with `campaign`. May be `{}` if no autoresponder field
needs to change.

campaign.description:
Required when updating a campaign-type newsletter. May be `{}`
(empty object) if no campaign-specific field needs to change —
its presence is what enables the update flow on the server.
Do not use it to change the campaign status: schedule, send,
archive and their reverse go through the dedicated
`/apps/api/v1/campaigns/{id}/...` endpoints.

id.description:
Newsletter ID. Must match the `{id}` path parameter. Required when
updating `name`, otherwise the duplicate-name check fails with 500.

default.description: Flag indicating if it's the default plan

single_optin.description: Uses single opt-in instead of double opt-in

warn_before_sending_without_can_spam_tag.description: Warns before sending without CAN-SPAM tags

mandatory.description: Flag indicating if the field is mandatory

is_pristine.description: Flag indicating if preferences are pristine

match_count.description: Number of contacts that match the segment

total_count.description: Total number of contacts in the list

default_sender.description: Flag indicating if it's the default sender

active.description: Flag indicating if the subscription is active

expired.description: Flag indicating if the subscription is expired

pending_payment.description: Flag indicating if there's a pending payment

Retrieves the list of campaigns.

**Filtering caveat:** when no filtering parameter is supplied, the
server falls back to a query that returns only campaigns whose status
is `SENT` or `ARCHIVED`. To list `DRAFT` or `SCHEDULED` campaigns you
must pass both `status` and `search_term` (the latter may be an empty
string), otherwise the result will silently exclude them. Use
`GET /apps/api/v1/campaigns/count` to get reliable per-status totals.

put.description:
Schedules a `DRAFT` campaign to be sent at a given date and time.
This is the only way to schedule a campaign: `campaign.status` sent to
`POST /apps/api/v1/newsletters` is ignored and new campaigns are always
created as `DRAFT`.

Prerequisites: the account is active, the sender (and reply-to, if set)
is verified, and the subscription can cover the recipients. Use
`PUT /apps/api/v1/campaigns/{id}/unschedule` to bring the campaign back
to `DRAFT`.

scheduled_time.description:
Local date and time of the send in the chosen
`timezone`, formatted `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`. Do not
append a UTC offset or `Z`: the offset comes from
`timezone`.

timezone.description:
Timezone ID from `GET /apps/api/v1/meta/timezones`.
Each timezone is a fixed UTC offset with no daylight
saving adjustment: pick the entry whose `offset`
matches the offset in force on the send date (e.g.
`+02:00` for Italy in summer, `+01:00` in winter).

200.description:
Campaign scheduled (`status: OK`) or rejected with `status: ERROR`
and a `message`: `cant_schedule` (campaign is not `DRAFT`),
`schedule_newsletter_account_not_active`,
`sender_address_unverified_with_link`, `newsletter_not_found`, or a
subscription-limit error.

put.description:
Starts sending a `DRAFT` (or `FAILED`) campaign immediately to all its
recipients. The request has no body.

Sending is asynchronous: `status: OK` means the campaign was queued.
Poll `GET /apps/api/v1/campaigns/{id}` for the final state. If the
dispatcher rejects it, the campaign ends in `FAILED` with a `reason`;
the most common one is `one_or_more_can_spam_tags_are_missing` (see
`CampaignCreate.html_body`).

200.description:
Campaign queued for sending (`status: OK`) or rejected with
`status: ERROR` and a `message` (e.g. `cant_send`,
`sender_address_unverified_with_link`).

put.description:
Sends a test email of the campaign to a single address. The campaign
status does not change. The sender (and reply-to, if set) must be
verified.

email.description: Email to send the test to

200.description:
Test queued (`status: OK`) or rejected with `status: ERROR` and a
`message` such as `invalid_email_address` or
`sender_address_unverified_with_link`.

put.description:
Cancels the scheduling of a `SCHEDULED` campaign and brings it back to
`DRAFT`. Returns `status: ERROR`, `message: cant_cancel_schedule` if the
campaign is not scheduled.

post.description:
Creates a new campaign or clones an existing one.

- **Create** (no `clone` query parameter): the body must include
  `instance_in.campaign` (object, may be empty `{}`). Without it the
  server responds with `200` and `{"status":"ERROR","message":"campaign_undefined"}`.
- **Clone** (`?clone=1`): the body only needs `instance_in.id` of the
  source campaign. Cloning a source campaign whose status is `SENT`
  is currently not supported and returns `500`.

parameters.description:
Set to `1` to clone an existing campaign instead of creating one.
Omit (or any other value) to create a brand-new campaign.
parameters.name: clone

id.description: ID of the source campaign to clone

local_datetime.description:
Optional client-side timestamp used by the cloning
flow to suffix the new campaign's name.

200.description:
Campaign created or cloned successfully. Note: the create flow may
also return a `200` body with `{"status":"ERROR","message":"campaign_undefined"}`
when `instance_in.campaign` is missing.

put.description:
Updates a newsletter (either a campaign or an autoresponder). This is
the correct endpoint to update campaign content fields like `name`,
`subject`, `html_body`, sender and lists. It does not schedule or send:
use `PUT /apps/api/v1/campaigns/{id}/schedule` and
`PUT /apps/api/v1/campaigns/{id}/send`.

**Important constraints:**

- This is a full replace, not a partial update: `name`, `subject`,
  `html_body`, `text_body`, `sender_id`, `reply_to_id` and the other
  newsletter fields are overwritten with `null` when omitted. Read the
  campaign with `GET /apps/api/v1/campaigns/{id}` and send back every
  field. A campaign left without `sender_id` can no longer be
  scheduled or sent.

- `instance_in` must include either a `campaign` or an `autoresponder`
  object (may be empty `{}`). Without one of them the request is
  silently ignored: the server returns `200 OK` but no field is
  persisted.
- When updating `name`, you must also include `id` inside `instance_in`
  (matching the path `{id}`). Otherwise the server's duplicate-name
  check fails and returns `500 General Error`.

200.description:
Newsletter updated successfully. **Warning:** a `200` does not
guarantee persistence — if `instance_in` did not include
`campaign` or `autoresponder`, the body change is ignored.

500.description:
Returned when updating `name` without duplicating `id` inside
`instance_in`, or on other server-side errors.

get.description:
Returns the per-contact engagement rows for a sent campaign — i.e. which
contacts opened, clicked, were delivered, unsubscribed, etc., together
with how many times and when.

**This is the endpoint to use for syncing opens/clicks to a CRM.** It is
distinct from the campaign audience: the audience (the contacts a
campaign targets) is returned elsewhere and does **not** support the
engagement flags below — passing them there has no effect by design.

Select which engagement slice you want by adding **one** flag parameter
with value `1` (e.g. `?open=1`). **At least one** of the engagement flags
(`open`, `click`, `deliver`, `unopen`, `unsubscribe`, `report`, `sent`,
`scheduled`) set to `1` is **required**. The flags are mutually
exclusive — pass only one per request. Alternatively, pass
`status=<value>` to filter by a specific raw delivery status (e.g.
`status=bounce`, `status=definite bounce`). Status values containing a
space must be URL-encoded (`definite%20bounce` or `definite+bounce`).

**Response format**: defaults to JSON. A `.csv` or `.json` suffix on the
path selects the format explicitly (e.g.
`/apps/api/v1/newsletters/{id}/contacts.csv?click=1`). For a full CRM
export, add `_mode=download` to bypass pagination and return every row.

**Caveats:**
- `_mode=download` has been observed returning `500` when the result set
  is empty. Guard against empty slices, or use the paginated form
  (without `_mode=download`), which returns `[]` safely.
- With `_mode=download` the rows expose `first_name`/`last_name` instead
  of the combined `name` field.

Filter by a specific raw delivery status (e.g. `bounce`,

Returns the count of contacts matching a given engagement slice, instead
of the rows themselves. Accepts the same flag/`status` parameters as
`GET /apps/api/v1/newsletters/{id}/contacts` (e.g. `?open=1`).
**At least one** of the engagement flags (`open`, `click`, `deliver`,
`unopen`, `unsubscribe`, `report`, `sent`, `scheduled`) set to `1` is
**required**; the flags are mutually exclusive — pass only one per
request.

**Note:** this endpoint has been observed returning
`500 {"message":"General Error"}` on some environments. When you only
need the total, you can also derive it by requesting the rows with
`_mode=download` and counting them. Prefer the rows endpoint for
reliable results.
